settings.name_in_paper: Hierarchical linear bandit with Gaussian rewards, sequential setting (|S_t|=1)
unmapped: Multi-task / meta-learning: m tasks with parameters theta_s ~ N(mu_*, Sigma_0), hyper-parameter mu_* ~ N(mu_q, Sigma_q); learner interacts with each task at most n times; one task per round, task order can depend arbitrarily on history
Learner knows mu_q, Sigma_q, Sigma_0 (hyper-prior and task-prior covariance)
settings.definition_quote:
\begin{align}
  \mu_*
  & \sim \cN(\mu_q, \Sigma_q)\,,
  \label{eq:gaussian hierarchical} \\
  \theta_{s, *} \mid \mu_*
  & \sim \cN(\mu_*, \Sigma_0)\,,
  & \forall s \in [m] \,,
  \nonumber \\
  Y_{s, t} \mid A_{s, t}, \theta_{s, *}
  & \sim \cN(A_{s, t}\T \theta_{s, *}, \sigma^2)\,,
  & \forall t \geq 1, \, s \in \cS_t\,,
  \nonumber
\end{align}
where $\Sigma_q \in \realset^{d \times d}$ and $\Sigma_0 \in \realset^{d \times d}$ are covariance matrices; $\mu_q$, $\mu_*$, $\theta_{s, *}$ are $d$-dimensional vectors; the set of actions is $\cA \subseteq \realset^d$; and the mean reward of action $a \in \cA$ is $r(a; \theta) = a\T \theta$. The reward noise is $\cN(0, \sigma^2)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Hierarchical linear bandit with Gaussian rewards, concurrent setting (|S_t| <= L)
unmapped: Multi-task hierarchical Gaussian model with m tasks, each interacted with at most n times
Concurrent: up to L tasks acted on per round; posterior updated only at end of round
Learner knows mu_q, Sigma_q, Sigma_0 and a basis {a_i} with lambda_d(sum a_i a_i^T) >= eta
settings.definition_quote: Now we investigate the concurrent setting, where the agent acts in up to $L$ tasks per round. ... There exist actions $\{a_i\}_{i = 1}^d \subseteq \cA$ and $\eta > 0$ such that $\lambda_d(\sum_{i = 1}^d a_i a_i\T) \geq \eta$.

settings.definition_quote: We start with a $K$-armed Gaussian bandit ... The covariance matrices are diagonal, $\Sigma_q = \sigma_q^2 I_K$ and $\Sigma_0 = \sigma_0^2 I_K$. We assume that both $\sigma_q > 0$ and $\sigma_0 > 0$ are known. The reward distribution of action $i$ is $\cN(\theta_{s, *, i}, \sigma^2)$, where $\sigma > 0$ is a known reward noise.

source.label: thm:sequential regret
source.quote: Let $|\cS_t| = 1$ for all rounds $t$ and $\cA \subseteq \realset^d$. Choose $\delta = 1 / (m n)$. Then the Bayes regret of \hierts is \Bregret(m, n) \leq d \sqrt{2 m n [c_1 m + c_2] \log(m n)} + c_3, where $c_3 = O(d^\frac{3}{2})$, ...

results.notes: c_3 is only given as O(d^{3/2}); recorded as a declared symbol. Regret summed over m tasks with at most n interactions each.
